questions.prompt: What is the capital city of New Zealand?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the New Zealand article.

questions.proof: The current capital city of the country is Wellington, and the largest city is Auckland.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with New Zealand?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture New Zealand on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geological origin” part of the New Zealand article.

questions.proof: New Zealand sits at the boundary between the Australian and Pacific continental plates.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of New Zealand?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the New Zealand article.

questions.proof: New Zealand (known as Aotearoa, in the Māori language) officially Commonwealth of New Zealand, is an island country in Oceania.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Zeeland is a province of the _____.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the New Zealand article, under the heading “Name”.

questions.proof: Zeeland is a province of the Netherlands.
